en.html:
Ichijou stood rigid beside me.

Understandable.

They had encountered one another at Enoshima, but this should be her first time facing it at close range. Confronted with such unmistakable abnormality, how could she not catch her breath?

What was different? The world was different.

So alien. So incomprehensible.

Something from another dimension.

A warrior—and something beyond warriors. One had to say it.

I too was speechless.

At Oyumi I had meant to seek a clue to Silver Star's whereabouts. An unexpected directly encounter, and like this... entirely outside my calculations.

While we were forced to imitate statues, the silver-white warrior remained composed. A glance at Ichijou—at Masamune—and a small tilt of the head. Then its gaze returned to me.

...Looking around, I saw armored remains besides Raichou Imagawa's. Dozens—more than that. Warriors. Dragoons. Every life cut off by skilled technique, unlike the frenzied deaths of the soldiers along our path.

Ordinary soldiers had destroyed themselves under mental contamination. Those warriors who withstood the wave had probably challenged Silver Star.

And been annihilated. More than a hundred masses of iron and flesh.

Loss ratio: one hundred to zero.

Alone over the battlefield, fresh with the reek of blood, the silver conqueror reigned. Not a drop of its own blood shed. Only a contented sigh.

A monster.

An aberration. A thing transformed. A demon.

Not human.

Kageaki Minato's sister, Hikaru Minato, had long since ceased to be human.

Having encountered it—

—I must bring it down.

Nothing else remained. If I meant to protect people as a human being, I had no path but to cut down my inhuman sister.

...I should have understood already. At the latest, when we met on Enoshima.

Yes.

Once, I had resolved to kill her.

But.

Even so...

Now I was speaking from my lingering attachment.

Its voice bright with expectation, Silver Star—what had once been Kageaki Minato's sister—asked that.

...Such a thing.

Not joking.

Not pretending to be wicked. Not even teasing.

Purely, sincerely.

I understood: it had no doubts.

After so many massacres. Sitting even now amid one. Declaring it had killed them all, not through enmity and conflict, but simply to kill.

Not even a doubt!

I had wanted, at least, to believe in madness. A terrible curse had driven my sister mad.

That had been denied.

Hikaru had explained, entirely logically, something she surely could not have faced if it were the origin of madness. Explained that it was not so.

I could call even that madness.

But I already knew. That would only be my own evasion.

A useless evasion. It would merely blunt the blade.

The blade that must cut down my sister.

What I needed was the reverse—

To face the truth.

en.html:
Unease stirred in my chest.

As though on a peaceful voyage. Fair wind, full sails. Gentle waves, clear sky. Nothing to fear. Peace was here, and promised to continue indefinitely—

Yet my heart beat a frantic alarm.

Desperate to warn me of a whale coming up from the seabed to attack.

胸がざわついた。

　それは例えて言うなら平穏な航海のなか。
　順風満帆、波は穏やか、空は晴天、憂うべき何物も
なく、平安は今ここにあり、しかもいつまでともなく
続くことが約束されている――

　なのに心臓は早鐘を打ち鳴らし、
　
　海底から鯨が襲来するのを警告しようと躍起なのだ。
